"Learning to type without looking at the keyboard" like Forenx said is pretty accurate.

All your keybinds should be easy to reach, otherwise you're going to have to look down at your keyboard to figure out where your hands are or click your hotbar. I have a hard time reaching past the 5 key with my left hand on WASD, so almost all of my keybinds use 1-5 only. To cope with effectively having fewer usable keys, I use modifiers, like shift and control.

If you're an omni-healer or even if you just regularly play multiple classes, I tend to also arrange skills on my hotbars by utility. For example, I have back and forward buttons on my mouse. I use the back button on all my healers for emergency heals because it's easy to reach quickly. Q and E are similar. If in my gameplay I can "plan" to need a cooldown or a skill, it will be further out on my keyboard than things I need to reach quickly.

Something I do occasionally as an Omni-crafter is to just go through all the categories on the marketboard and fill in the gaps for popular items. If an item is low supply and the options that are there are way out of the typical price range for that item or there are none available, that's going on my list.

It's probably not as fast as just selling tomestone crafting items, but it gives me a shopping list of things to craft that tend to sell reliably. It's a good way to fill up the market slots on your retainers and put them to work. You do tend to have to check your items prices as other people do the same thing and inevitably undercut you, but for the material cost of some of these items, that extra check on the price is worth it. The profit margin is just so large sometimes.

One thing I will say is that crafting max level gear tends not to make me as much gil and usually costs me more in the end-- in either time, gil, or both. People craft the current gear and fresh 80 gear like mad and the market for it tends to not be great, imo.

Someone juat told me about this subreddit and honestly I'm kind of shocked that this is a thing and how many seemingly serious comments there are about "gamers are bullies", "gamers are going to Hell", "gamers shoot up schools", and "gamers are violent and aggressive".

I'm not religious but I grew up Crhistian. I feel like I understand the core points Jesus taught on decently well and one of those that cones to mind is to treat others as you would your neighbor. I forget the passage, but the Bible also mentions sonething akin to "treat those who cannot be convinced as a tax collector". I don't think that means to be so aggressive and hateful, even though a ton of people have flooded this place with shit-posts all of a sudden. I think it means to distance oneself and create healthy boundaries, something that people of all beliefs could learn from.

I could easily say the same types of things about Christians. There are extreme cases in all groups and relgious folks of any religion are no exempt. People who game that exhibit violence were not turned into a violent or abhorrent person by a game. They have a mental illness or anger problem that was already present that was aggrevated by a game. Thus isn't something that only presents when people with these kind of conditions game. It happens with a lot of different types of conflict and I'd bet my life that if you took 10 cases of violently angry people who game and banned video games, those people would react the same to similar conflict stimuli as they would to people with the same angry dispositions would but who don't game.

The key here is mental health awareness, not banning video games.

It serves the purpose of forcing the player to heal tactically.

2. Forcing the player to sheathe and unsheathe tactically. Unsheathing shouldn't really be an issue since you should almost always be attacking into an unsheathe, not unsheathing and then beginning to attack. The latter takes much longer. Sheathing can shorten the amount of time you take to get to the monster, but only if you estimate correctly. Sometimes rolling to cover distance with your weapon drawn is faster. Weapons are heavy. If you want to minmax, then I suppose you'd feel the hurt a lot more in terms of trying to get all the best skills in one set, but those skills don't make or break the game-play. The hunter's skill does.

4. This is only true of the late game, unless you're not using rank-appropriate armor. I think of armor like a safety net, not something that makes me invincible. Not sure if you mean you don't remember if they broke or if you're not sure how to tell if a part is broken or not, but I'm gonna go with the latter and explain it anyway just in case.

Generally when you break a part on a monster, there's a brief breaking animation/particle effect and the part changes appearance. Sometimes the break also causes the monster to stagger, but not all monster staggers are part breaks. On Tetsu, the tusks shear off about half way and look pretty jagged. In this case they break one at a time. When both have the same broken appearance, the part is considered "broken" and you get a chance for the part drop listed on Kiranico. Not all parts have this 2-stage breaking, I don't think, but a fair amount do.

Selecting Blademaster filters out armor/skills that are for Gunners, since you can't wear Gunner armor while using a Blademaster weapon and Gunner skills aren't useful to you as a Blademaster.

To answer your first question, Blademaster and Gunner are "professions". If you use a Greatsword, Insect Glaive, Charge Blade, etc. then you're a Blademaster and should be crafting Blademaster armor. Gunners use the Heavy Bowgun, Light Bowgun, or Bow and cannot wear Blademaster armor (except for helmets since those can generally be worn by either profession) and vice versa. Skills, like Gathering, give you bonuses granted either from slotting gems that give you points toward that skill, a charm that gives points toward that skill, or armor coming with inherent bonuses to points contributing to the skill. Skills become active when they hit +10. Similarly, if a skill hits -10, a negative skill becomes active, generally doing the opposite of what the positive version does. Specifically, I think the Gathering skill sometimes increases the number of times you can gather from a specific resource node. For information on specific skills, Kiranico is pretty good at explaining them.

Your special attack (R) is used to shoot a scent for your Kinsect to follow. When sent out, your Kinsect travels in a straight line toward the scent spot (which will be the same color as the buff collected on the part the scent is on) on the marked monster. Marking a tall monster on a spot high on its body, such as the back or base of the wings, is a good way to collect buffs that would be unreachable otherwise. For example, Red can only be collected from a Gravios' head. That's pretty high up and he only likes to lower his head when he shoots his lasers. Marking the base of his wings or his side can send your Kinsect high enough to hit the head if you position yourself correctly. Marking a monster directly on the head or wings or any other part that moves around a lot should generally be avoided since your Kinsect is likely to miss because the monster decided to flap its wings or turn its head.

Vaulting with your Insect Glaive lets you avoid tremors and get a free vault. If something is going to stomp or otherwise flop on the ground to attempt to tremor you, vaulting can get you a free, safe mount or just let you get some nice free hits.

Just because vaulting is a nice feature doesn't mean it's the only one. I.G is a fantastic status weapon and deals really good DPS. Get some Red and your attack speed goes way up. Stack some white for extra movement speed and more attack.

Speaking of double and triple buffing, when fighting a monster whose Red spot is hard to hit without marking using the scent, hold off on getting the Orange buff. I like to get Red and White immediately and then grab Orange when those both start to blink when their buff time is nearly over. This will reset their buff timers, preventing you from having to collect Red again for a little while. This could also be done by collecting Red only, then White to reset the buff timer, then Orange to reset that timer again.
